children: Cipla shares traded marginally lower on Friday amid a strong broader market, after the drugmaker’s partnership with China’s Qilu Pharmaceutical. The new partnership for a Keytruda biosimilar is expected to strengthen its oncology and specialty portfolio in the US.

The Cipla stock was down 0.27 percent at around Rs 1,391 in late-morning trade, taking the company’s market capitalisation to more than Rs 1.12 lakh crore. The shares have declined 7.4 percent so far in 2026, compared with an 8.6 percent fall in the Nifty 50.

The marginal decline came despite strength in the broader market. At 11:05 am, the Sensex was up 595 points, or 0.78 percent, at 76,748.32, while the Nifty gained 93 points, or 0.39 percent, to 23,966.80.

Morgan Stanley maintained its 'Underweight' rating on Cipla with a target price of Rs 1,218 per share, implying a downside of around 13 percent from the previous close. The brokerage said Cipla’s exclusive partnership with Qilu to license and commercialise the Keytruda biosimilar QL2107 in the US strengthens its oncology and biosimilars portfolio and supports its specialty growth strategy.

However, Morgan Stanley also flagged intense competition in the segment, saying that at least 13 pembrolizumab biosimilars are currently under development.

Cipla on September 3 announced that its wholly owned subsidiary Invagen Pharmaceuticals had entered into a strategic licensing and supply partnership with Qilu Pharmaceutical for QL2107, a biosimilar to pembrolizumab, sold under the Keytruda brand.

Under the agreement, Qilu will be responsible for developing QL2107, securing regulatory registration and supplying the product, while Cipla will lead its commercialisation in the US. Pembrolizumab is an oncology therapy, and Cipla said the biosimilar could help broaden access to advanced cancer treatment while lowering treatment costs.

"This partnership reflects Cipla's confidence in the long-term potential of biosimilars and supports our strategy to build a strong oncology-focused portfolio," Cipla Managing Director and Global CEO Achin Gupta said.

Qilu Pharmaceutical has a pipeline comprising more than 50 biosimilars and over 130 innovative drugs. The partnership combines the Chinese drugmaker's research, development and manufacturing capabilities with Cipla's commercial presence in the US.

title: Cipla shares slip after Keytruda biosimilar deal with Qilu, as competition worries weigh; Morgan Stanley cautious
